subject: Optima Health — model shortlist, context spec, and traffic estimate
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@optimahealth.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Optima Health — initial model shortlist + traffic snapshot for implementation planning

Samira / Optima team — thanks again for the demo last week. As discussed, I’m starting the handoff to our implementation and modeling leads so we can lock in a recommendation for the PoC and the Dedicated sizing baseline. Attached are the rough MAU/usage numbers you shared and the sample prompts you dropped in the repo. Summary below — please review and correct if anything is off.

Quick summary (from Optima notes):
- Primary surface: clinical note summarization + patient-facing Q&A (search + refinement)
- Expected ramp: 20k MAU at 6 months, 60k MAU steady-state at 12–18 months (per attached spreadsheet)
- Interaction pattern: ~2 queries/user/day during peak adoption (mix of short clarifications and longer doc summarization)
- Average context: many requests include a 3–5 page discharge note; we expect 1–3 docs per request after preprocessing (chunking)

Initial asks for the implementation team:
1) Model shortlist for PoC + recommended default for production (tradeoffs: latency vs quality vs cost)
2) Context length needs and recommended chunking approach (system vs user context, doc embeddings, KV cache)
3) Token-volume estimate (daily / monthly) with peak concurrency assumptions and a baseline Dedicated GPU recommendation

Proposed shortlist (internal suggestion; we’ll finalize after your confirmation):
- Llama-2-13b-chat (4-bit quant) — good latency/cost balance; strong for instruction-following
- Falcon-40B-instruct (16k context) — higher quality for long-form summarization but higher cost
- GPT‑NeoX-20B (mixed-precision) — reliable middle-ground, better deterministic outputs on templates

Notes on context: many of the discharge notes are semi-structured and compress to ~1,200–1,800 tokens each after tokenization. For complex summarization flows we expect active context windows of ~3–6k tokens (system + 2–3 docs). If Optima will supply embeddings store + retrieval, we can reduce active context to 1–2k tokens for most queries and do a single follow-up streaming pass for long summaries.

Preliminary token math (please confirm numbers in the CSV):
- Peak DAU (6mo ramp): 20,000 users; steady-state: 60,000 users
- Queries/day (6mo): 20k * 2 = 40,000 requests/day
- Avg tokens per request (system + context + response): 1,200 tokens
- Daily tokens (6mo): ~48M tokens/day -> ~1.44B tokens/month
- Peak concurrency (99th pct): assume 100 QPS sustained bursts -> throughput needs for batching / Dedicated sizing below

Attachments: optima_mau_estimates.csv, sample_prompts.jsonl, draft_SoW_v0.pdf

Next steps: Connor / Grace — can you pick this up and propose a concrete PoC model, one production fallback, and a Dedicated capacity baseline (GPU count + recommended instance family) aimed at the 6-mo ramp? Samira — please confirm the MAU numbers and whether Optima will provide an embeddings index (we should discuss retention / PII handling if so).

Thanks — Lauren
--
Lauren Bishop
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0192

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Samira Khan <samira@optimahealth.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Feb 2028 10:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Optima Health — initial model shortlist + traffic snapshot for implementation planning

Thanks Lauren — picking this up. A few clarifying points from my side before I finalize recommendations:

1) Retention and data flow: Will Optima persist full original notes in your environment, or will you rely on us to keep a short-term KV cache and downstream ATLAS logs? If you retain full notes we need to discuss redaction/PII hashing for the embeddings pipeline.

2) SLAs and fallback: Are there SLA commitments for the PoC window? That affects whether we recommend Hosted tier for flexibility vs Dedicated right away.

3) Response quality target: For the Q&A surface, what % accuracy (vs human labels) do you need to consider the model production-ready? Even a ballpark helps (e.g., >85% extractive F1).

Prelim model stance: I agree with the shortlist Lauren suggested. My recommendation for the PoC is: Llama-2-13b-chat (4-bit quant) as default PoC model, with Falcon-40B-instruct held as a higher-quality fallback (batch/async for heavy summarization). For production, if Optima wants near-human summarization on long documents we should offer Falcon or similar 40B-class models behind Dedicated capacity. Llama-13b quant gives great infer cost savings for interactive Q&A.

Quick sizing ask: I’ll draft a baseline using 40k requests/day and 1.2k tokens/request. If Optima confirms embeddings availability we can cut active context by ~50% for interactive flows which materially reduces token spend.

I’ll schedule a 30-min tech sync with your engineering lead — Samira, does next Wednesday 9:30am PT work?

Connor
Lead ML Engineer, Implementation
connor_obrien@redwood.ai

From: Samira Khan <samira@optimahealth.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Optima Health Platform <eng@optimahealth.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Feb 2028 08:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Optima Health — initial model shortlist + traffic snapshot for implementation planning

Thanks Lauren / Connor — confirm the numbers are a good starting point. A few clarifications from Optima:

- We will retain full notes in our private S3. For the PoC we can provide a sanitized subset. Long-term we prefer the embeddings store to sit in our VPC (we can expose retrieval via a private endpoint).
- Compliance: SOC 2 Type II and HITRUST are relevant for our auditors. We need the Private deployment option for production and an audit trail for all model calls.
- Quality target: for Q&A we want >= 88% on our labeled dev set; for summarization we accept a slightly lower ROUGE but need consistent extractive highlights.

On the operational side, we do expect heavy document summarization during business hours (10am–4pm ET) with spikes after discharge bundles. The average discharge packet compresses to ~1.5k tokens; when users request cross-doc summaries it can hit 5k+ active tokens.

I can do Wed 22 Feb 9:30am PT (that’s Thurs 23rd for us) for a tech sync. I’ll also upload a sanitized dump and add a short doc describing retention and PII fields.

Best,
Samira
Head of Product, Optima Health

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira@optimahealth.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Feb 2028 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Optima Health — initial model shortlist + traffic snapshot for implementation planning

Connor / Lauren — based on the confirmed clarifications from Samira I ran the sizing & cost back-of-envelope. Below is a recommended PoC and a conservative production baseline intended for a 6-month ramp to 20k DAU (Optima’s near-term goal).

PoC recommendation (90-day):
- Model: Llama-2-13b-chat (4-bit) on Hosted Dedicated group (to start quickly)
- Context strategy: client-hosted embeddings + retrieval for static clinical knowledge; active context window ~2k tokens for Q&A, single-pass 6k streaming for long summaries
- Traffic: assume 40k requests/day; avg tokens/request 1,200 -> 48M tokens/day (~1.44B/month)
- Trial capacity: 1 dedicated node (NVIDIA H100 equivalent) with autoscale to 2 for peak business hours; target P99 latency <700ms for Q&A (with batching)

Conservative production baseline (6–12mo):
- 3 Dedicated nodes (H100 family) with autoscaling rules to add 1 node per 100 QPS sustained beyond baseline; persistent KV cache & prefix caching enabled to reduce duplicate tokenization cost
- Model strategy: default Llama-13b-4q for interactive paths; Falcon-40B-instruct on async pipeline for long summaries (batch/worker pool)
- Cost estimate: with 1.44B tokens/month active at Llama-13b quantized rates we estimate ~ $Xk/month (I’ll convert to a precise figure for the proposal) — note embeddings retrieval cutting active context by 40–55% would reduce that by a similar factor
- Rollout plan: 2-week canary (10% traffic), monitor model regression metrics (ROUGE / extractive recall) and latency/cost dashboards; if regressions >5% revert to Falcon fallback for the affected workload

Attachments: example sizing sheet and a short checklist for SOC 2/HITRUST artifacts (we will need the SOC attestation and network topology diagram from Optima).

Connor — I’ll prepare a short slide pack with these bullets + an operations runbook for the kickoff. Samira — can you confirm the sanitized dump upload and whether your security team prefers a vendor assessment before the PoC?

Thanks — Grace
Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.ai

From: Samira Khan <samira@optimahealth.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Feb 2028 15:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Optima Health — initial model shortlist + traffic snapshot for implementation planning

All — this looks great. Confirming the sanitized dump will be uploaded by EOD Thursday and the security team will schedule a short vendor questionnaire call next Monday. We’re comfortable starting the PoC on Llama-2-13b-chat (4-bit) with Falcon-40B as a fallback.

Next step: Connor — please send the calendar invite for Wed 22 Feb 9:30am PT. Lauren — I’ll look over the SoW draft and leave comments in the Doc.

—Samira
